reviews.frank_statement: positional SQL binding is vulnerable to schema/arity drift and current FRANK contains a concrete SQL binding defect
reviews.counterhypothesis: compiler-known positional lowering is equally safe if exact schema contract identity is frozen and checked before execution
reviews.falsifier: a matched schema-evolution mutation suite shows no reliability difference between named and positional lowering under equivalent preflight, or named lowering creates unacceptable cost/semantic ambiguity
adversarial_checks: new NOT NULL/no-default target column causes named execution to fail too; compile-time schema preflight must reject it rather than masking incompatibility
reviews.reason: named-field lowering is strongly supported as the safer default at evolving schema boundaries, but it is not a substitute for contract/schema preflight and need not replace positional lowering inside a frozen verified ABI

reviews.frank_statement: ClayGraph projection can leave disappeared or superseded relations apparently CURRENT across graph epochs
reviews.counterhypothesis: the existing invalidation queue or runtime projector can guarantee stale-edge removal without a distinct COMPLETE_SNAPSHOT projection contract in ClayCode IR
reviews.falsifier: target-machine projector tests prove all complete projections already retract omitted prior-current relations under crash/replay/concurrency without needing an explicit completeness contract
independent_checks: E2B isolated replication with stale A-C relation
differential/incremental computation prior art supports explicit change propagation rather than assuming omission semantics
adversarial_checks: PATCH projections must not interpret omission as deletion; retraction is required only when the producer declares complete-domain snapshot semantics
reviews.reason: the stale-edge failure class is executable and reproduced, but the language-level fix should be projection completeness/retraction semantics rather than an unconditional negative-delta rule for every update

reviews.frank_statement: FRANK materialization lineage is not sufficiently bound to admitted repository identity before state/open/current use
reviews.counterhypothesis: existing provenance fields plus an external boot admission gate are sufficient and a ClayCode AdmissionIdentity record would duplicate responsibility
reviews.falsifier: an exact H1 boot/replay suite proves current provenance and gate semantics reject divergent/unadmitted/materializer-mismatched state without additional typed admission identity
independent_checks: SLSA provenance model independently supports binding produced artifacts to source/build lineage, but does not establish FRANK-specific field design
adversarial_checks: do not make repository identity itself semantic truth; admission only authorizes which source/materialization may be treated as CURRENT
reviews.reason: typed admission/materialization lineage is justified as an interface requirement, while exact record fields and placement remain an implementation question until target-machine differential tests

reviews.frank_statement: revisioned work and freshness-aware capability state are needed for dynamic multi-organ execution
reviews.counterhypothesis: generic ClayCode records/interfaces plus existing V9 semantics already express the requirement; new work/cap.resolve grammar primitives add no measurable value
reviews.falsifier: parser/model/runtime benchmarks show dedicated syntax materially reduces errors/context/cost while preserving semantics and portability
adversarial_checks: current G9 V3 already has generic record/rule/effect structures and V9 stores work revisions/capability freshness explicitly
reviews.reason: there is no current executable evidence that new grammar keywords beat the existing typed-record/runtime representation
